workItems.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
workItems.description: Two below-threshold surface code memories on Willow, a distance-7 code and a distance-5 code integrated with a real-time decoder, indicate device performance that, if scaled, could realize the operational requirements of large-scale fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.

workItems.title: Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit
workItems.description: Reports measurement of logical qubit performance scaling across several code sizes and an experimental demonstration in which quantum error correction begins to improve performance with increasing qubit number.

workItems.title: Qd-tree: Learning Data Layouts for Big Data Analytics
workItems.description: Experiments over benchmark and real workloads show that a qd-tree can provide physical speedups of more than an order of magnitude compared to current blocking schemes, and can reach within 2X of the lower bound for data skipping based on selectivity, while providing complete semantic descriptions of created blocks.

workItems.title: Measurement-Induced State Transitions in a Superconducting Qubit: Within the Rotating Wave Approximation
workItems.description: Superconducting qubits typically use a dispersive readout scheme, where a resonator is coupled to a qubit such that its frequency is qubit-state dependent. Measurement is performed by driving the…

workItems.title: Observation of constructive interference at the edge of quantum ergodicity
workItems.description: The dynamics of quantum many-body systems is characterized by quantum observables that are reconstructed from correlation functions at separate points in space and time.

workItems.title: Overcoming leakage in quantum error correction
workItems.description: Demonstrates a distance-3 surface code and distance-21 bit-flip code on a quantum processor for which leakage is removed from all qubits in each cycle, and reports a tenfold reduction in the steady-state leakage population of the data qubits encoding the logical state.

workItems.title: Scaling and logic in the colour code on a superconducting quantum processor
workItems.description: Research on quantum error correction and colour-code scaling and logic using a superconducting quantum processor.

workItems.title: Resisting High-Energy Impact Events through Gap Engineering in Superconducting Qubit Arrays.
workItems.description: Studies gap engineering in superconducting qubit arrays to resist high-energy impact events and support quantum error correction.

workItems.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor.
workItems.description: Implements cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develops a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound magic state fidelity.

workItems.title: Phase transitions in random circuit sampling
workItems.description: By implementing an algorithm for random circuit sampling, experimental and theoretical results establish the existence of transitions to a stable, computationally complex phase that is reachable with current quantum processors.

workItems.title: Elementary gates for quantum computation.
workItems.description: U(2) gates are derived, which derive upper and lower bounds on the exact number of elementary gates required to build up a variety of two- and three-bit quantum gates, the asymptotic number required for n-bit Deutsch-Toffoli gates, and make some observations about the number of unitary operations on arbitrarily many bits.

workItems.title: Mixed-state entanglement and quantum error correction.
workItems.description: It is proved that an EPP involving one-way classical communication and acting on mixed state M (obtained by sharing halves of Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen pairs through a channel) yields a QECC on χ with rate Q=D, and vice versa, and it is proved Q is not increased by adding one-way classical communication.

workItems.title: Open Quantum Assembly Language
workItems.description: OpenQASM represents universal physical circuits over the CNOT plus SU(2) basis with straight-line code that includes measurement, reset, fast feedback, and gate subroutines that is used to implement experiments with low depth quantum circuits.

workItems.title: Purification of noisy entanglement and faithful teleportation via noisy channels.
workItems.description: Upper and lower bounds on the yield of pure singlets (|Ψ−⟩) distillable from mixed states M are given, showing D(M)>0 if ⟨Ψ−|M|Ψ−⟩>1/2.

workItems.title: Experimental quantum cryptography
workItems.description: An apparatus and protocol designed to implement quantum key distribution is described, by which two users exchange a random quantum transmission, consisting of very faint flashes of polarized light, which remains secure against an adversary with unlimited computing power.

workItems.title: Quantum nonlocality without entanglement
workItems.description: We exhibit an orthogonal set of product states of two three-state particles that nevertheless cannot be reliably distinguished by a pair of separated observers ignorant of which of the states has…

workItems.title: Entanglement-assisted capacity of a quantum channel and the reverse Shannon theorem
workItems.description: In the classical analog of entanglement-assisted communication - communication over a discrete memoryless channel (DMC) between parties who share prior random information - one parameter is sufficient, i.e., that in the presence of prior shared random information, all DMCs of equal capacity can simulate one another with unit asymptotic efficiency.

workItems.title: Unextendible product bases and bound entanglement
workItems.description: An unextendible product basis (UPB) for a multipartite quantum system is an incomplete orthogonal product basis whose complementary subspace contains no product state. We give examples of UPBs, and…

workItems.title: Trading Classical and Quantum Computational Resources
workItems.description: A purely classical algorithm is proposed that can simulate a Pauli-based computation (PBC) on n qubits in a time 2^(c n) poly(n) where c≈0.94.

workItems.title: OpenQASM 3: A Broader and Deeper Quantum Assembly Language
workItems.description: OpenQASM 3 is extended to include timing, pulse control, and gate modifiers, which create a multi-level intermediate representation for circuit development and optimization, as well as control sequence implementation for calibration, characterization, and error mitigation.

workItems.title: Demonstration of low-overhead quantum error correction codes
workItems.description: Demonstrates the feasibility of performing quantum error correction with long-range coupled superconducting processors, demonstrating the viability of low-overhead quantum error correction.

workItems.title: Experimental quantum adversarial learning with programmable superconducting qubits
workItems.description: Experimental demonstration of the vulnerability of quantum machine learning models against adversarial noises and a defense strategy using a programmable superconducting quantum processor.

workItems.title: Digital Simulation of Projective Non-Abelian Anyons with 68 Superconducting Qubits
workItems.description: Experimental quantum digital simulation of projective non-Abelian anyons and their braiding statistics with up to 68 programmable superconducting qubits arranged on a two-dimensional lattice; implements single- and two-qubit logic gates through elementary Pauli gates.

workItems.title: Non-Abelian braiding of Fibonacci anyons with a superconducting processor
workItems.description: Research on non-Abelian braiding of Fibonacci anyons with a superconducting processor.

workItems.title: Creating and controlling global Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger entanglement on quantum processors
workItems.description: Research on creating and controlling global Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger entanglement on quantum processors.

workItems.title: Many-body Hilbert space scarring on a superconducting processor
workItems.description: Reports observation of quantum scarring, a weak-ergodicity-breaking mechanism, in many-body quantum systems using a superconducting processor.

workItems.title: Quantum ensemble learning with a programmable superconducting processor
workItems.description: Introduces AdaBoost.Q, a quantum adaptation of the classical adaptive boosting algorithm designed to enhance quantum classifiers' learning capabilities and prediction accuracy.

workItems.title: Digital quantum simulation of Floquet symmetry-protected topological phases
workItems.description: Digital quantum simulation of Floquet symmetry-protected topological phases in quantum many-body systems away from equilibrium.

workItems.title: Demonstrating quantum error mitigation on logical qubits
workItems.description: Demonstrates zero-noise extrapolation applied to quantum error correction circuits on superconducting processors, reducing logical errors and advancing early fault-tolerant quantum computing.

workItems.title: Measuring the Spectral Form Factor in Many-Body Chaotic and Localized Phases of Quantum Processors.
workItems.description: Uses the spectral form factor to capture universal spectral fluctuations as signatures of quantum chaos.

workItems.title: Beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes
workItems.description: A beam search decoder for quantum low density parity check (LDPC) codes based on a beam search heuristic guided by belief propagation (BP) is proposed, suggesting one might only need three 32-core CPUs to decode a trapped ion quantum computer with 1000 logical qubits.

workItems.title: Quantum error correction for long chains of trapped ions
workItems.description: This work designs syndrome extraction circuits tailored to the ion chain model, a syndrome extraction tuning protocol to optimize these circuits, and constructs new quantum codes that outperform the state-of-the-art for chains of about 50 qubits.

workItems.title: Real-time decoder for a MegaQuOp quantum computer using a single CPU
workItems.description: An end-to-end real-time decoding stack for a universal fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computer architecture capable of decoding real workloads with millions of logical gates over hundreds of logical qubits is demonstrated.

workItems.title: Correction of chain losses in trapped ion quantum computers
workItems.description: This work proposes a solution to the chain loss problem based on a quantum error correction code distributed over multiple long chains, beacon qubits within each long chain to detect the loss of a chain, and a decoder adapted to correct a combination of circuit faults and erasures after beacon qubits convert chain losses into erasures.

workItems.title: Soft decoding for quantum LDPC codes with experimental validation
workItems.description: A soft beam search decoder for quantum low-density parity-check codes that uses internal decoder data as a confidence metric, removing the need for extra computation is introduced.

workItems.title: PriorTilt: Decoding quantum LDPC codes with sparse perturbations of belief propagation priors
workItems.description: PriorTilt is introduced, a variant of BP obtained by selectively perturbing a small fraction of its prior log-likelihood ratios using offsets determined by recent posterior and outgoing-message statistics, while preserving the same message-passing rules.

workItems.title: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum memories over a 2xL array of qubit modules
workItems.description: This work proves that quantum LDPC codes such as BB codes can maintain their performance in a distributed setting while using solely one simple connector: a cyclic shift, whereas previous results for qubit arrays are limited to CSS codes.

workItems.title: Distributed Quantum Error Correction Based on Hyperbolic Floquet Codes
workItems.description: Under the circuit-level noise model, it is demonstrated through simulations that distributed hyperbolic Floquet codes offer good performance with achievable local and non-local fidelities of approximately 99.97% and 99%, respectively, which shows that distributed quantum error correction is not only possible but also efficiently realisable.

workItems.title: Logical gates on Floquet codes via folds and twists
workItems.description: This work shows how two techniques from static quantum error-correcting codes can also be implemented on Floquet codes, and shows that these logical operations are robust, featuring a performance that is close to the baseline set by a quantum memory benchmark.

workItems.title: Lecture hall graphs and the Askey scheme
workItems.description: We establish, for every family of orthogonal polynomials in the q-Askey scheme and the Askey scheme, a combinatorial model for mixed moments and coefficients in terms of paths on the lecture hall.

workItems.title: Entanglement measures of bipartite quantum gates and their thermalization under arbitrary interaction strength

workItems.title: Impact of local dynamics on entangling power

workItems.title: Reinforcement Learning Control of Quantum Error Correction
workItems.description: Presents a reinforcement learning framework for quantum error correction; numerical simulations of large codes with tens of thousands of control parameters confirm scalability and optimization speed independent of system size.

workItems.title: Non-Markovian relaxation spectroscopy of fluxonium qubits
workItems.description: Studies parasitic two-level systems in superconducting qubits, a leading source of decoherence, including relaxation behavior.

workItems.title: Arbitrary controlled-phase gate on fluxonium qubits using differential ac Stark shifts
Observation of disorder-induced superfluidity
workItems.description: Studies the emergence of states with long-range correlations in a disordered landscape, where disorder typically suppresses particle mobility required for long-range coherence.

workItems.title: Multifractal and Glassy Signatures of Non-Ergodic 2D Quantum Dynamics
workItems.description: Theoretical and numerical study of ergodicity and localization in disordered, interacting quantum systems in two spatial dimensions.

workItems.title: Correlation of Lifetime Fluctuations in Superconducting Qubits
Demonstration of the Two-Fluxonium Cross-Resonance Gate
workItems.description: Describes the superconducting fluxonium qubit's potential for high-fidelity quantum gates, based on long coherence times and strong anharmonicity at the half flux quantum sweet spot.

workItems.title: A 40-nm Cryo-CMOS Quantum Controller IC for Superconducting Qubit
workItems.description: Presents a cryo-CMOS quantum controller IC for superconducting qubits, with a globally synchronized clock system that internally generates different local oscillator frequencies.

workItems.title: A Cryo-CMOS Controller IC With Fully Integrated Frequency Generators for Superconducting Qubits
workItems.description: Presents a cryo-CMOS controller IC with fully integrated frequency generators for superconducting qubits.

workItems.title: 34.4 A Cryogenic Controller IC for Superconducting Qubits with DRAG Pulse Generation by Direct Synthesis without Using Memory
workItems.description: Presents a cryogenic controller IC for superconducting qubits with DRAG pulse generation by direct synthesis without using memory.

workItems.title: A 5.5mW/Channel 2-to-7 GHz Frequency Synthesizable Qubit-Controlling Cryogenic Pulse Modulator for Scalable Quantum Computers
workItems.description: Presents a qubit controller IC based on direct synthesis, consisting of six independently working pulse modulators utilizing the same local oscillator frequency, and proposes sinusoid shaping.

workItems.title: A 40 nm Cryo-CMOS Homodyne-Demodulation Readout SoC for Superconducting Qubits
workItems.description: Presents a cryo-CMOS readout SoC based on a homodyne demodulation architecture with an integrating receiver.

workItems.title: A Quantum Controller IC With DRAG Generation in 40-nm Cryo-CMOS for Scalable Superconducting Quantum Computing
workItems.description: Presents a cryo-CMOS controller that supports derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) pulses without requiring internal memory, using trigonometric relations.

workItems.title: A 7-10b Programmable Cryo-CMOS TI-SAR ADC for Multichannel Qubit Readout with On-Chip Background Inter-Channel Mismatch Calibrations
workItems.description: Presents a cryo-CMOS dynamic-precision time-interleaved SAR ADC for frequency-division-multiplexing-based qubit readout, with on-chip background calibration engines to compensate for dynamic inter-channel mismatch.

workItems.title: A 5.5mW/Channel 2-to-7 GHz Frequency Synthesizable Qubit-Controlling Cryogenic Pulse Modulator for Scalable Quantum Computers
workItems.description: Presents a qubit controller IC based on direct synthesis, with six independently working pulse modulators utilizing the same local oscillator frequency and a sinusoid-shaping proposal.

workItems.title: Competitive and cost effective high-k based 28nm CMOS technology for low power applications
workItems.description: Presents a cost-effective 28nm CMOS technology for low-power applications based on a high-k, single-metal-gate-first architecture, reporting a 2.4x area reduction from 45nm technology.

workItems.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor.
workItems.description: Implements cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develops a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound magic state fidelity; experimentally establishes magic state cultivation as a viable solution to a quantum computing challenge.

workItems.description: Senior Research Scientist in the Micromodules Group, Optics and Optical Communications Group and Optical Measurements Group, working in the R&D of optoelectronic modules and instruments, such as autofocus systems for mobile phones, high power laser modules, visibility meters for infrared region, laser rangefinders, LED modules for displays, optical sensors for electronic water taps, fibre optic in-vessel viewing system for a fusion reactor, imaging lidar for space applications, miniature CMOS cameras, fibre optic transceivers and wavelength tunable laser modules. I started the series of the R&D projects funded by the European Space Agency aiming to the qualification of high-speed fibre-optic transceiver modules for intra-satellite data communications. Today the first type of these modules is ready for commercialization. I carried out studies for the Doctoral Thesis titled: "Wavelength tunable laser module for fibre optic communications."​ The short external cavity diode laser used an electrically controlled silicon micromachined (MEMS) Fabry-Perot interferometer chip as the tuning element. The single-mode fibre coupled modules operated at the 1,540-nm wavelength band and were able to produce either multimode or single-mode tuning. These modules were the world's first directly electrically modulated external cavity lasers and had an electrical modulation bandwidth of 600 MHz. For more information, please read: IEEE Photonics Technology Letters, Vol. 16, No. 4, pp. 1164–1166; Electronics Letters, Vol. 40, No. 14, pp. 871–872; IEEE Transactions on Advanced Packaging, Vol. 28, No. 1, pp. 121–127, and VTT Publications 528, 171 p. + app. 11 p. ISBN 951-38-6375-1.

workItems.title: Research Scientist, VTT
workItems.description: Research Scientist in the Optical Sensors and Instruments Group, working in the R&D of optoelectronic systems including offset plate measuring sensors, thermal sensitive press plate testing environment and density meter for printing industry; spectrographs, lightness meters and LED-based illumination modules for paper industry; spectrographs and optical sensors for reading x-ray photographs for medical industry; laser pulse measurement systems for military applications; and imaging lidar and laser-altimeter for space applications. I wrote my Licentiate Thesis titled: "Fibre optic in-vessel viewing system for a fusion reactor". A viewing system was designed and a prototype realized for the in-vessel inspection of the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) that is now under construction in Saint-Paul-lez-Durance, France. The viewing was based on the line scanning principle, and the designed system consisted of ten identical units installed on top of the reactor at 36° intervals. Each device contained an illuminating laser, beam steering mirrors, and viewing probe with insertion mechanics. The diffuser optics created a vertically oriented light stripe onto the vessel surface that was viewed by the imaging optics, consisting of 16 modules altogether covering horizontal and vertical field-of-views of 2° and 162°. The optical images were transferred to CCD cameras via coherent fibre arrays. The viewing probes rotated at a constant angular speed of 1°/s and pictures were taken at 0.01° intervals. The complete picture of the vessel interior was generated in 6 min. Under optimum conditions, the minimum resolvable feature size at a 3 m distance was smaller than 1 mm. For more information, please read: Review of Scientific Instruments, Vol. 73, No. 7, pp. 2616–2623 and Fusion Engineering and Design, Vol. 58 - 59, pp. 513–516.

data.headline: A very excited researcher, pursuing research in the intersection of Signal processing and Machine Learning, I love to study, explore and research on the mathematical foundations of Signal Processing and Machine Learning Theory. I love to develop algorithms for various applications based on rigorous mathematical basis. I am interested to pursue research in understanding the theoretical foundations of Deep Learning. The recent ideas of mechanistic interpretation of Deep Learning (especially the Transformers Architecture) are something that interest me the most. I have a background in developing Signal Processing algorithms and in teaching (Probability, Control Theory, Digital Signal Processing, and Machine Learning) from my masters and doctoral degrees. My PhD at University of Florida involved working with physics informed matrix factorization for waves and connections to approximate eigendecompositions. I was advised by Prof. Joel Harley. I worked for Marvell Semiconductor Inc., in the SSD DSP Architecture team where I developed channel models for NAND SSDs. At Marvell, I also worked on evaluating various state of the art LLMs and explored Retrieval Augmented Generation for simple applications: through which I developed a deep understanding of the Transformer architecture and many elegant ideas in modern Natural Language Processing (NLP). I am presently a postdoctoral researcher in the Multi-source Probabilistic Inference Research group in the Department of Computer Science at University of Helsinki. In the process, I am transitioning from a Bayesian connoisseur to a Bayesian practitioner. On the applications side, I am stepping into the intersection of computational biology and machine learning: specifically in microbial community modeling.
